+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copy a packaged steam.desktop, rewriting every Exec=/usr/bin/steam to a wrapper.
+#
+#   steam-desktop-override <src> <dst> <wrapper>
+#
+# Called from home.nix's steamDesktopOverride activation entry, which passes
+# /usr/share/applications/steam.desktop, ~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop
+# and the `steam` wrapper it builds. See the wrapper's comment in home.nix for why
+# Steam needs to be launched through one at all.
+#
+# A script here, rather than the whole file mirrored into home.nix the way
+# Zoom.desktop is: steam.desktop is ~400 lines -- Comment= in 27 languages, then
+# nine Desktop Actions each with its own set -- and the only lines that need to
+# differ are the ten Exec=. Deriving the file from the pacman one also means a
+# steam.desktop changed by a package update is picked up by the next `hms` instead
+# of silently drifting from a copy in this repo.
+#
+# An unreadable source is success, not failure. That keeps "which hosts have
+# Steam" a question only system/packages.<host> answers -- the same split
+# system/thermald-setup uses for its own enable half -- so this can run
+# unconditionally on every host, including the Darwin one, and do nothing.
+set -eu
+
+src=${1:?source desktop file}
+dst=${2:?destination desktop file}
+exe=${3:?wrapper to point Exec= at}
+
+[ -r "$src" ] || exit 0
+
+# Two anchored patterns rather than one with \b, which is a GNU sed extension:
+# activation runs on Darwin too, and while the readable-source check above means
+# sed is never reached there today, a pattern that only works under GNU sed is a
+# trap for whoever moves this next. Anchoring also does the job \b was for --
+# neither matches a hypothetical Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo.
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
+tmp=$(mktemp "$dst.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
+
+sed -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam |Exec=$exe |" \
+    -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam\$|Exec=$exe|" \
+    "$src" > "$tmp"
+
+# 0644 explicitly: mktemp makes it 0600, and a desktop file the launcher cannot
+# read is the same as no override at all.
+chmod 0644 "$tmp"
+mv -f "$tmp" "$dst"
+trap - EXIT

+#
+# The bug it exists for, measured on shiori 2026-09-28:
+#
+#   xdg-user-dir: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/libc.so.6: undefined symbol:
+#   __pointer_chk_guard, version GLIBC_PRIVATE

+# Steam shells out to `xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD` to find the download directory.
+# `~/.nix-profile/bin` sits ahead of `/usr/bin`, and xdg.userDirs.enable puts
+# nix's xdg-user-dirs in the profile, so that resolves to the nix binary -- which
+# Steam's runtime then forces against the host's /usr/lib/libc.so.6, a glibc that
+# does not export the GLIBC_PRIVATE symbol a nix-glibc build wants. The wrapper
+# puts the host's own helpers first so Steam gets /usr/bin/xdg-user-dir.
+#
+# The half that is easy to get wrong is the other direction, which is why it has
+# cases of its own: the profile must NOT be dropped from PATH. `xdg-open` exists
+# ONLY in the nix profile on this box (Arch's xdg-utils is not installed), and it
+# is how Steam opens a link in a browser. A wrapper that sanitised PATH by
+# stripping nix would trade a broken download path for broken links.
+#
+#   ./tests/steam-env.sh                 # builds the wrapper, then tests it
+#   ./tests/steam-env.sh /path/to/steam  # tests one you already have
+#
+# The wrapper is resolved from homeConfigurations.shiori specifically, not from
+# $(cat /etc/hostname): steam is a shiori-only package, and the cases are about
+# the wrapper's own logic, so there is no reason they should only be runnable on
+# the one box.

+echo "PATH=$PATH"
+echo "GIO_EXTRA_MODULES=${GIO_EXTRA_MODULES-<unset>}"
+echo "GIO_MODULE_DIR=${GIO_MODULE_DIR-<unset>}"
+echo "XDG_DATA_DIRS=${XDG_DATA_DIRS-<unset>}"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copy a packaged steam.desktop, rewriting every Exec=/usr/bin/steam to a wrapper.
+#
+#   steam-desktop-override <src> <dst> <wrapper>
+#
+# Called from home.nix's steamDesktopOverride activation entry, which passes
+# /usr/share/applications/steam.desktop, ~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop
+# and the `steam` wrapper it builds. See the wrapper's comment in home.nix for why
+# Steam needs to be launched through one at all.
+#
+# A script here, rather than the whole file mirrored into home.nix the way
+# Zoom.desktop is: steam.desktop is ~400 lines -- Comment= in 27 languages, then
+# nine Desktop Actions each with its own set -- and the only lines that need to
+# differ are the ten Exec=. Deriving the file from the pacman one also means a
+# steam.desktop changed by a package update is picked up by the next `hms` instead
+# of silently drifting from a copy in this repo.
+#
+# An unreadable source is success, not failure. That keeps "which hosts have
+# Steam" a question only system/packages.<host> answers -- the same split
+# system/thermald-setup uses for its own enable half -- so this can run
+# unconditionally on every host, including the Darwin one, and do nothing.
+set -eu
+
+src=${1:?source desktop file}
+dst=${2:?destination desktop file}
+exe=${3:?wrapper to point Exec= at}
+

+
+# Two anchored patterns rather than one with \b, which is a GNU sed extension:
+# activation runs on Darwin too, and while the readable-source check above means
+# sed is never reached there today, a pattern that only works under GNU sed is a
+# trap for whoever moves this next. Anchoring also does the job \b was for --
+# neither matches a hypothetical Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo.
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
+tmp=$(mktemp "$dst.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
+

+    -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam\$|Exec=$exe|" \
+    "$src" > "$tmp"

+# 0644 explicitly: mktemp makes it 0600, and a desktop file the launcher cannot
+# read is the same as no override at all.
+chmod 0644 "$tmp"
+mv -f "$tmp" "$dst"
+trap - EXIT

+echo "GIO_EXTRA_MODULES=${GIO_EXTRA_MODULES-<unset>}"
+echo "GIO_MODULE_DIR=${GIO_MODULE_DIR-<unset>}"

+  W=/nix/store/fake-steam/bin/steam
+  out="$D/out/applications/steam.desktop"   # a directory that does not exist yet
+  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" "$W" 2>"$D/err"; then
+    ok "rewrite succeeds and creates the destination directory"
+  else
+    bad "rewrite succeeds and creates the destination directory" "$(sed 's/^/      /' "$D/err")"
+  fi
+
+  chk() { # chk <case> <expected exact line>
+    if grep -qxF "$2" "$out" 2>/dev/null; then ok "$1"
+    else bad "$1" "    wanted: $2"; fi
+  }
+  chk "main Exec= is rewritten, %U kept"        "Exec=$W %U"
+  chk "an action's steam:// argument is kept"   "Exec=$W steam://store"
+  chk "a bare Exec= with no argument is rewritten" "Exec=$W"
+  chk "a translated Name= is untouched"         "Name[uk]=Крамниця"
+  chk "a translated Comment= is untouched"      "Comment[ja]=Steam 上でゲームを管理＆プレイするためのアプリケーション"
+
+  # Anchoring earns its keep twice: a key that merely ends in the same path, and a
+  # binary whose name merely starts with "steam".
+  chk "X-Not-Exec= is not rewritten"            "X-Not-Exec=/usr/bin/steam %U"
+  chk "Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo is not rewritten" "Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo --wat"
+
+  # Nothing but Exec= may move. This is the case that would catch a future pattern
+  # widened past what it meant to touch.
+  changed=$(diff "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" | grep '^[<>]' | grep -cv '^[<>] Exec=/usr/bin/steam\|^[<>] Exec=/nix/store/fake-steam' || true)
+  if [ "$changed" = 0 ]; then ok "no line other than an Exec= differs"
+  else bad "no line other than an Exec= differs" "$(diff "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" | sed 's/^/      /')"; fi
+
+  # The launcher runs as this user but reads the file like any other; mktemp's 0600
+  # would leave an override that silently does not apply under some launchers.
+  mode=$(stat -c '%a' "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
+  if [ "$mode" = 644 ]; then ok "the override is mode 0644"
+  else bad "the override is mode 0644" "    got $mode"; fi
+
+  # The host gate. Every host runs this activation entry, so a box without Steam --
+  # or the Darwin one -- must come out clean and quiet, not failed.
+  rm -f "$D/absent.desktop"
+  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/absent.desktop" "$D/never" "$W" 2>"$D/err2"; then
+    if [ ! -e "$D/never" ] && [ ! -s "$D/err2" ]; then
+      ok "an unreadable source exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing"
+    else
+      bad "an unreadable source exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing" \
+        "    created: $([ -e "$D/never" ] && echo yes || echo no), stderr: $(cat "$D/err2")"
+    fi
+  else
+    bad "an unreadable source exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing" "    exited non-zero"
+  fi
+
+  # Re-running over an existing override is what every `hms` after the first does.
+  before=$(cat "$out")
+  bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" "$W" 2>/dev/null
+  if [ "$before" = "$(cat "$out")" ]; then ok "re-running is idempotent"
+  else bad "re-running is idempotent" "    second run changed the file"; fi
+
+  # No temp file may survive next to the real one; a launcher scanning the
+  # directory would pick up steam.desktop.XXXXXX as a second entry.
+  leftovers=$(find "$(dirname "$out")" -name 'steam.desktop.*' | wc -l)
+  if [ "$leftovers" = 0 ]; then ok "no mktemp leftovers beside the override"
+  else bad "no mktemp leftovers beside the override" "    found $leftovers"; fi
+fi
+
+echo
+[ "$skips" -gt 0 ] && echo "$skips skipped"
+if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "all $n cases passed"
+else
+  echo "$fails of $n cases FAILED"
+fi
+exit $((fails > 0))

# dotfiles

Home Manager configuration for `sauyon`.

## New machine setup

For a blank machine (ISO, disk, base Arch install), see
[docs/new-host.md](docs/new-host.md). The steps below assume Arch is already
running.

```bash
# 1. Clone into ~/devel/dotfiles
mkdir -p ~/devel
git clone https://github.com/sauyon/dotfiles ~/devel/dotfiles

# 2. If this is a new host, add a homeConfigurations entry for it in flake.nix
#    (hostname, gui, gpu). Otherwise the matching entry already exists.

# 3. Install Nix
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
  | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm

# 4. Source Nix and trust mise
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh
mise trust ~/devel/dotfiles/mise.toml

# 5. Apply (flake attr matches hostname)
nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch --flake ~/devel/dotfiles#$HOST
```

After the first switch, `home-manager switch` is available directly.

## Applying changes: `hms`

`hms` is the normal way to switch. It does **not** build locally by default — it
pushes, waits for the commit's CI run, then switches, which turns the switch into
a download of the closure the runner already built and pushed to attic.

```bash
hms              # push, wait for the run, then switch
hms --local      # skip CI and build here (the old `home-manager switch` alias)
```

Things it deliberately refuses rather than works around:

- **A dirty tree.** CI builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch is one CI
  can never reproduce. Commit, or use `--local`.
- **A stale checkout.** If `origin/master` has commits you do not, it says so and
  stops — rebasing is your call, and waiting on a run for a SHA that is not
  `origin/master` would be waiting on the wrong build.

It falls back to a local build, with a note, when the host has no CI job (mari)
or when the commit touched nothing `nix-home.yml`'s `paths:` filter matches. On a
red run it prints the job's actual `error:` lines, not just a status.

Why this is worth a wait: see `docs/ci-nix-home.md`. The short version is that
the runner has far more of everything than these boxes, and its output is
bit-identical to what a local build would produce.

## Tests

Nothing here has a suite; the exception is anything whose logic is a model of
someone else's, where a comment claiming the model is right proves nothing.

```bash
./tests/hyprlock-faillock.sh     # builds the script, then drives 33 cases
./tests/system-packages.sh       # sources system/pacman.sh, drives 21 cases
./tests/thermald-setup.sh        # drives 8 cases against system/thermald-setup
./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh   # drives 13 cases against the live generated zsh config
./tests/steam-ui-scaling.sh      # evaluates 3 hosts, drives 4 cases
./tests/steam-env.sh             # builds the steam wrapper, drives 26 cases
```

`hyprlock-faillock` (in `home.nix`) reproduces pam_faillock's two tally windows
to tell the lock screen whether the account is locked out. The cases drive the
real built script through its `FAILLOCK_BIN` / `FAILLOCK_CONF` / `FAILLOCK_USER`
seams, so a stub reader supplies synthetic tally records -- no real failed
logins, no waiting out a real ten-minute lockout.

`system/pacman.sh` holds the parts of `system/deploy`'s package convergence that
model someone else's rules: the list format plus the per-host overlay, and the
single `Include` line appended to `/etc/pacman.conf` (whole-line matched, so the
stock config's commented-out examples don't read as "already enabled"). The
cases source it and run against a temp tree through its `SUDO` seam, then hand a
copy of this host's real `pacman.conf` to `pacman-conf` to confirm pacman does
glob an `Include` and does register a `[multilib]` section reached through one --
the assumption the whole drop-in design rests on. Nothing writes to `/etc`, and
no case needs root.

`system/thermald-setup` (run from `system/deploy`) is the *enable* half that a
package list cannot express: `pacman -S` installs a unit, it does not start one.
Which hosts want thermald is decided upstream of it, by `thermald` appearing in
`system/packages.<host>` — so the script's own gate is just "is it installed",
and a host whose list never asked for it is one it never touches. The cases drive
the real script with stub `pacman`/`sudo`/`systemctl` on `PATH`, asserting both
halves: a host without the package does nothing at all, and a converged host
escalates zero times.

The `_ghostty_saved_ps1` priming in `zsh.nix` is a model of ghostty's
`ghostty-integration`: it pre-sets variables private to that script so its own
`ps1_changed` guard fires on the first precmd, which is what stops the PS1
rewrite that corrupts powerlevel10k's `PROMPT` into a literal `}}`. Rename those
variables upstream and nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
symptom is the artifact coming back. The cases render the *live generated* config
in a pty -- both the injected and plain startup paths -- and assert the `}}` is
gone with the line and still returns without it, so a workaround that has quietly
stopped working fails out loud, and so does one that has become unnecessary.

`STEAM_FORCE_DESKTOPUI_SCALING` (in `home.nix`) models Steam's side of a bargain
Hyprland can't enforce: `xwayland.force_zero_scaling` hands X11 clients real
pixels and no DPI hint, and Steam's CEF UI reads neither `Xft.dpi` nor
`GDK_DPI_SCALE`, so on a scaled panel it draws tiny until told its own factor.
The cases evaluate three hosts and derive every expectation from the config
itself — the var must equal the scale that host's eDP-1 monitor rule asks for,
and be unset where there is no such rule — so the pair can't drift apart
silently, which is the only way this fails. A fourth case asserts a scaled host
still exists, since otherwise all three would pass vacuously.

The `steam` wrapper (in `home.nix`) and `home/steam-desktop-override` model the
one place nix's profile and a pacman-installed app genuinely collide. Steam shells

# Evaluate one option out of a host's config. nix eval's stderr is pure noise on

# story on a broken one, so it is held back and printed only when the eval fails

# when the host does not define it, so absence is an ordinary expected value and
# not an eval failure a case has to special-case.

  eval_option "$1" home.sessionVariables \
    | jq -r --arg v "$VAR" '.[$v] // "<unset>"'

  fails=$((fails+1))

echo

			# Older .desktop implementations used the execute bits as

				# implementation reloads it
				touch "$DESKTOP_DIR/$STEAMPACKAGE.desktop"

Review of `10fabaf..HEAD` (3aff29e) + the uncommitted README.md hunk. Everything below was checked against the real `shiori` filesystem read-only; I did not run the test script (it writes temp files).

---

## 1. SPEC COMPLIANCE — no Critical, one Important, one nit

The change addresses exactly (a) and (b) and nothing else. `PATH` prepend fixes (a); `unset GIO_EXTRA_MODULES` fixes (b); the `.desktop` rewrite exists only so the wrapper is actually reached. No unrelated files touched.

**Launch-path coverage — all five real paths reach the fix:**

| path | reached? | why |
|---|---|---|
| terminal `steam` | yes | wrapper is in shiori's `home.packages` → `~/.nix-profile/bin/steam`, which precedes `/usr/bin` |
| app launcher (.desktop) | yes | override at `~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop`; that dir currently holds only `claude-code-url-handler.desktop`, `RimWorld.desktop`, `Zoom.desktop`, `mimeapps.list` — nothing contends |
| `steam://` URL | yes | verified in the profile's `xdg-open` (`/nix/store/REDACTED.2.1/bin/xdg-open`, lines 177 and 207): `search="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-…}:${XDG_DATA_DIRS:-…}"`, first hit wins. `x-scheme-handler/steam=steam.desktop` exists only in `/usr/share/applications/mimeinfo.cache:17`; `~/.local/share/applications/mimeinfo.cache` does not exist and `mimeapps.list` has no steam entry. The comment's precedence claim is correct. |
| tray "restart Steam" | yes, indirectly | `/usr/lib/steam/steam` sets `STEAMSCRIPT="$(cd "${0%/*}" …)/${0##*/}"`, i.e. `/usr/bin/steam` when the wrapper execs it — so a restart re-execs `/usr/bin/steam` and *bypasses the wrapper script*, but inherits the wrapper's environment, so both fixes survive. Worth a sentence in the comment; a reader currently has to work this out. |
| game launched by Steam | yes | Steam's own generated shortcut `~/.local/share/applications/RimWorld.desktop` is `Exec=steam steam://rungameid/294100` — bare `steam`, resolved from the session PATH where the profile wins. pressure-vessel passes env through, which is also why the `GIO_EXTRA_MODULES` unset reaches sniper. |

**Important — the PATH prepend's blast radius is much wider than `xdg-user-dir`.** `export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH"` puts the host ahead of the nix profile for *every* binary Steam and its whole descendant tree resolves by name — Proton helper scripts, `bash`, `python`, `gamemoderun`, `mangohud`, `git`, anything a game's launch options invoke. Where both an Arch and a nix copy exist, the Arch one now silently wins inside Steam only. The comment argues the prepend-vs-sanitise tradeoff well, but not this one, and it is the larger of the two. An alternative that fixes (a) at its actual scope — e.g. a `xdg-user-dir` shim dir, or prepending only `/usr/bin` — isn't considered. Not wrong, but the comment claims "Prepending is also what spares this a list of which helpers to redirect" as a pure win when it is a tradeoff.

**nit — two launch paths bypass the wrapper, neither exists today.** `/usr/lib/steam/steam` lines 195-199 copy `/usr/lib/steam/steam.desktop` (`Exec=/usr/bin/steam %U`) into `$XDG_DESKTOP_DIR` on bootstrap — `~/desktop` does not exist, so it never fires. And if the user ever enables "Run Steam on startup", Steam writes `~/.config/autostart/steam.desktop` with `Exec=/usr/bin/steam` (not present now). Both would silently reintroduce the bug. Worth one line acknowledging them.

---

## 2. VERIFICATION — no Critical, four Important, plus two things I checked and found sound

The suite is genuinely good: the stub reports the environment it received rather than the wrapper's intent, so a wrapper that sets vars but never execs fails every case; and the stub's `${GIO_EXTRA_MODULES-<unset>}` (bare `-`, not `:-`) correctly distinguishes unset from set-but-empty, which is what makes the "must be unset" case real rather than cosmetic.

**Important — the `STEAM_BIN` default is never exercised.** Every one of the 13 wrapper cases goes through `run`, which always sets `STEAM_BIN="$D/stub"`. Mutate `${STEAM_BIN:-/usr/bin/steam}` to any other path and all 26 cases still pass. The one fact the wrapper exists to guarantee — that it ends up at the pacman binary — has no coverage.

**Important — nothing covers the `home.nix` wiring.** `nix eval` is used only to *locate* the wrapper. No case asserts the `steamDesktopOverride` activation entry exists, or that its three arguments are `/usr/share/applications/steam.desktop`, `${config.xdg.dataHome}/applications/…`, `${steam}/bin/steam`. Change the third argument to `/usr/bin/steam`, or point `dst` at `~/.nix-profile/share/applications` (which the comment itself says loses to `/usr/share`), and 26/26 pass while the fix is dead. `tests/steam-ui-scaling.sh` established the config-eval pattern for exactly this failure mode — that convention is not carried over here.

**Important — "no mktemp leftovers beside the override" is near-vacuous relative to what its comment implies.** The comment frames it as protecting the cleanup path, but `mv -f "$tmp" "$dst"` removes the temp on success, so deleting `trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT` from the script passes this case. It only catches a `cp`-instead-of-`mv` mutation. The `trap` is untested; so is the atomicity property the temp-file dance exists for (no case makes `sed` fail and then asserts `$dst` is untouched).

**Important — the `grep -cv` pipeline's comment is wrong about what it catches.** Mechanics first, since you asked me to trace it: `diff | grep '^[<>]'` then `grep -cv '^[<>] Exec=/usr/bin/steam\|^[<>] Exec=/nix/store/fake-steam'`. BRE `\|` is a GNU extension and the test's `grep` is GNU grep 3.12 (`/usr/bin/grep`; the interactive `grep` here is a ugrep alias, but that does not apply in a non-interactive bash script) — I confirmed the alternation with a synthetic 3-line diff: returns `1` for one non-matching line. `|| true` is genuinely needed, because `grep -c` exits 1 when the count is 0. So the pipeline works. But both patterns are unanchored on the right, so `> Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo --wat` matches `^[<>] Exec=/usr/bin/steam` and `> Exec=/nix/store/fake-steam/bin/steam --wat` matches the second — meaning the case's stated purpose, "the case that would catch a future pattern widened past what it meant to touch", is precisely what it does *not* catch. The widening is caught, but by the separate `Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo is not rewritten` chk. No hole in the suite; the comment is false. (A mutation that touched `X-Not-Exec=` *would* be caught here, since `^[<>] Exec=` cannot match `> X-Not-Exec=`.)

**Important — the skip conditions let the one case that models the actual bug vanish silently, and the repo already has the antidote.** `xdg-user-dir resolves outside the nix store` skips unless both `/usr/bin/xdg-user-dir` and `~/.nix-profile/bin/xdg-user-dir` exist.
